mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.05 t-stat) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months in at least 80% of out-of-sample episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.05 t-stat) when GDPC1 YoY change falls below -2% in at least 70% of out-of-sample episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6.5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.05 t-stat) during periods when UNRATE exceeds 6.5% for two consecutive months in at least 60% of out-of-sample episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces earnings visibility and triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls > -0.5% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.05 t-stat) when INDPRO declines by more than -0.5% for three consecutive months in at least 65% of out-of-sample episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the federal funds rate and a fall in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.3% in the same month signals a restrictive monetary policy coinciding with weakening inflation, which increases real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises and CPIAUCSL falls > -0.3% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.05 t-stat) when FEDFUNDS rises and CPIAUCSL falls > -0.3% in the same month in at least 60% of out-of-sample episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS growth > 0.4% month-over-month) and a rise in housing starts (HOUST > 5% month-over-month) signals strengthening household demand, which boosts consumption and capital expenditure, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS growth > 0.4% and HOUST growth > 5% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.05 t-stat) when PAYEMS and HOUST both rise above thresholds in the same month in at least 65% of out-of-sample episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the unemployment rate below 4.5% for four consecutive months signals an overheating labor market, which raises wage pressures and inflation expectations, prompting the Federal Reserve to tighten policy and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.05 t-stat) when UNRATE remains below 4.5% for four consecutive months in at least 60% of out-of-sample episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent year-over-year increase in real personal savings (proxied by RSAFS growth > 3% for three consecutive months) indicates households are accumulating cash rather than spending, which reduces near-term consumption demand and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS growth > 3% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.05 t-stat) when RSAFS grows by more than 3% for three consecutive months in at least 65% of out-of-sample episodes.
